newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Dutch say restructuring programme main fisheries priority.
newsitem.headline: Dutch say restructuring programme main fisheries priority.

text.p: Agreement on a fourth multi-annual programme (MAGP4) will be the main fisheries priority under the Dutch EU Presidency, Dutch farm minister Jozias Van Aartsen said on Tuesday.

Van Aartsen, briefing the European Parliament's fisheries committee, said that technical conservation measures and a North Sea conference on the integration of environmental and fisheries policies were other priorities.
"These are the three main (fisheries) pillars but the only decision during the first half of 1997 is likely to be on MAGP4," Van Aartsen said.
A two-day fisheries council is planned in Luxembourg on April 14-15 to try and hammer out agreement on controversial plans for sharp cuts in fishing fleets between 1997-99.
If no deal is reached in April, the Dutch will make a final bid to clinch a deal at another Luxembourg Fisheries Council on June 23.
The previous five-year EU fisheries restructuring programme expired at the end of 1996.

But the Commission agreed in December 1996 that fishermen may continue to receive EU aid for laying up vessels and leaving the industry on condition that a new programme is agreed by the end of April, 1997.

On technical conservation measures, Van Aartsen said there were two main objectives in Commission proposals present on June 26, 1996. Firstly, to improve the effectiveness to stop fishing of young fish, those from threatened stocks and fishing at certain times of the year.
He urged the European Parliament to give its opinion quickly.
"It's vitally important to help move things forward," he said.

On the North Sea conference, Van Aartsen said ministers from countries with North Sea coastlines will meet in Bergen, Norway, from March 13-16 to prepare for a fifth conference to integrate environmental and fisheries policies.
Relations with non-EU countries was another issue raised by Van Aartsen.
He said negotiations on fisheries accords with Poland and Russia will start in 1997.
Talks would also be held with Norway on the management of joint North Sea herring and mackerel stocks.
Pressed by Euro MPs to end the impasse over proposals to ban all driftnet fishing by the end of 1997, Van Aartsen made no promises.
"I cannot give rise to exaggerated hopes," he said.
